title: NATS (JetStream)
description: Is the shared NATS hub (CT 131) up, is JetStream healthy and is every consumer keeping up? Open it after a Nats* alert or an HttpProbeFailed on the nats health URL, when Kubeletto's events stall, and weekly for storage.

panels.title: Is the hub up and JetStream healthy?
Hub up
panels.description: The server answers its health URL with JetStream enabled (healthz?js-enabled-only=true; rule HttpProbeFailed, 5 minutes, critical for this critical-tier host) and the exporter scrape works (rule TargetDown). DOWN means Kubeletto's event flow (builds, deployments, notifications) is stalled. Next: 'systemctl status nats' in CT 131 and the Server log row.

panels.title: JetStream enabled
panels.description: The exporter's own view of the server: JetStream on or off. The health probe in the tile beside it already fails (rule HttpProbeFailed) when the server is up without JetStream; this tile says which half is wrong. No separate alert.

panels.title: Account storage, fullest
panels.description: Real bytes stored by the fullest JetStream account over its limit (8 GiB for kubeletto), not the streams' reservations. Red from 80 % is rule NatsAccountStorageHigh (30 minutes); at 100 % publishes to its streams are refused. Tiny today: streams are capped by messages and age.

panels.title: Largest consumer backlog
panels.description: Messages waiting for the most-behind durable consumer. Red above 1000 is rule NatsConsumerBacklog (15 minutes): that consumer's app stopped consuming (down, stuck, or a poison message). The Consumers table names it.

panels.title: Messages being redelivered
panels.description: Messages JetStream has had to deliver again because a consumer did not ack in time, summed over every consumer (a gauge of messages currently redelivering). 0 is healthy; a number that stays above 0 is a poison message or a slow handler. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Root disk used
panels.description: CT 131's root disk, which holds the JetStream file store, from the Proxmox API. Red from 80 % is rule NatsDiskFilling (30 minutes). The CT has no node_exporter, so this is the only disk series. The Disk row has the history.

panels.title: Leaf links up
panels.description: Leaf-node connections to the hub. Kubeletto's cluster joins as one leaf, so 1 is healthy and 0 means the cluster is cut off from the hub (every client count reads 0 anyway: apps never connect directly). No alert mirrors it: a dead leaf shows first as a growing consumer backlog.

panels.title: Slow consumers, 1 h
panels.description: Connections the server cut off for not reading fast enough, in the last hour (its slow-consumer counter). Should be 0: a slow reader loses messages that are not in JetStream. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Messages per second, in and out
panels.description: Messages the server received and delivered per second, over every connection (here: the one leaf link). Out runs above in because a message can be delivered to several subscribers and JetStream consumers. A flat zero while Kubeletto runs means the leaf or the apps are silent. No alert rule.

panels.title: Bytes per second, in and out
panels.description: Payload bytes received and delivered per second. Events are small (tens of bytes per second at rest). A step up means a bulk publisher; compare with the stream sizes below. No alert rule.

panels.title: JetStream API requests and errors per second
panels.description: Requests to JetStream's management API (stream and consumer info, ack and pull handling) and the ones that failed. Errors should be 0; a line above 0 is a client asking for a stream or consumer that does not exist or that refuses the request. No alert rule.

panels.title: Is every consumer keeping up, and is storage safe?
Account storage used, share of its limit
panels.description: Real bytes stored by each JetStream account over its limit (max_file in proxmox/opentofu/nats.tf). The dashed line is 80 %, rule NatsAccountStorageHigh (30 minutes). Usually the cause is a stream with no max_age or max_bytes, or a consumer that never acks. Near zero today.

panels.title: Consumer backlog, by consumer
panels.description: Messages waiting for each durable consumer. The dashed line is 1000, rule NatsConsumerBacklog (15 minutes). A line that climbs and does not come back is an app that stopped consuming; a brief spike after a deploy is normal. The labels name the stream and consumer (all of them are Kubeletto's today).

panels.title: Redelivered and unacked messages
panels.description: Over every consumer: messages being redelivered (a handler timed out or crashed) and messages delivered but not yet acked. A short burst of awaiting-ack is a handler working. Redelivered that stays above 0 is a poison message (it ends in the DLQ_* stream if the app has one). The Consumers table below names the consumer. No alert rule.

panels.title: Stream size, by stream
panels.description: Bytes held by each stream. Each is capped by its own limit (500 MiB) and by age, so a line that climbs steadily toward the cap is a stream that is not being consumed or trimmed. Streams at zero are hidden. Their sum is the account storage above. No alert rule.

panels.title: Messages published per second, six busiest streams
panels.description: Messages appended per second to the six busiest streams, derived from each stream's last sequence number (the exporter has no publish counter). When the hub is quiet all six read 0 and which six are drawn is arbitrary. A stream that should be busy and is flat is a publisher that stopped. No alert rule.

panels.title: Streams
panels.description: Every stream: messages and bytes held, its own limits (blank = unlimited: the DLQ_* dead-letter streams) and how many consumers read it. A stream near its message or byte limit discards old messages or refuses new ones, per its discard policy. A stream with 0 durable consumers is only written to; several are today. No alert rule.

panels.title: Root disk used, over time
panels.description: CT 131's root disk, which holds the JetStream file store, from the Proxmox API. The dashed line is 80 %, rule NatsDiskFilling (30 minutes). Fix: find the stream that grew (du in /var/lib/nats/jetstream), or grow disk_gb in proxmox/opentofu/nats.tf (online).

panels.title: JetStream reservations, share of the server maximum
panels.description: Disk the streams have reserved with a byte cap, over the server's JetStream storage limit (10 GiB). Reservations are promises, not bytes in use: past 100 % the server refuses to create another capped stream. Not the NatsDisk rules' number: those read real bytes. No alert rule.

panels.title: Server memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the nats-server process. Tens of MB for this workload; growth that does not come back is a leak or a huge number of subscriptions. The CT's own memory is on the Host and guest board. No alert rule.

panels.title: Server CPU
panels.description: CPU the nats-server process uses, in percent of one core, as the server reports it. Near zero at rest; sustained tens of percent means message volume or a hot consumer. No alert rule.

panels.title: Leaf connection from the Kubeletto cluster
Leaf links and client connections
panels.description: Connections to the hub by kind. Kubeletto's cluster joins through one leaf link, so 'leaf links' should hold at 1 and a drop to 0 is the cluster cut off (the network path to the hub, or the hub restarting). Direct client connections and cluster routes stay at 0 by design: this is a single server and apps reach it only through the leaf. No alert rule.

panels.title: Slow consumers and stale connections
panels.description: Connections the server dropped because a reader fell behind (slow consumers, and the share that were the leaf link) or stopped answering pings (stale), counted per window. Should stay at 0. A leaf slow consumer means the cluster side cannot keep up with what the hub sends. No alert rule.

panels.title: NATS: errors and warnings
panels.description: Server lines tagged [ERR] or [WRN] by nats-server, plus anything the journal marks error or critical. A few warnings at start-up (JetStream recovery, a leaf reconnect) are normal; a stream of them is the story behind an alert. Not checked by --verify-live.
